model_type: Classical LSTM neural network OCR engine (Tesseract.js v5+ with LSTM-only OEM)
privacy_compliance: 100% private and on-premise. Processes image in server memory with zero external transmission; fully compliant with PHI isolation and local data governance standards.
on_device_binary_size_impact: 0 MB on mobile app bundle in current client-server setup. If embedded locally in React Native, requires ~30MB-50MB for native binaries and eng+fil traineddata files.
printed_label_accuracy: Moderate (75-84% character accuracy on clean, planar labels; drops below 60% on low-contrast, colored, or curved pharmaceutical containers).
handwriting_recognition: Extremely poor (<20% accuracy on handwritten physician prescriptions; frequently generates symbol noise like pipes, backslashes, and random ASCII punctuation).
multilingual_code_switching_support: Limited. Requires eng+fil language models. Raw character recognition frequently garbles Filipino ligatures (na, ng) and accented text; relies heavily on post-processing regex rules.
curved_surface_and_glare_tolerance: Very low. Planar assumption leads to severe distortion on cylindrical pill bottles and character fragmentation under metallic blister pack glare.
tabular_timetable_parsing: Weak. Lacks spatial document understanding; multi-dose timetable rows and columnar hospital schedules frequently merge into unparseable text streams.
hallucination_under_degraded_input: Low generative hallucination. It does not invent words out of thin air, but degraded inputs produce garbage character strings that can trigger false positive regex matches.
latency_seconds: 4.2 to 8.5 seconds on multi-core CPU (worker initialization, canvas rasterization, and LSTM matrix passes).
ram_peak_footprint: 280MB to 450MB peak resident memory per active Tesseract worker in Node.js.
cost_profile: 100% Free and open-source (Apache 2.0 license). Zero API subscription fees, zero per-image operational cost.
react_native_compatibility: Currently integrated via Node.js API endpoint (POST /medications/ocr-draft). Decouples mobile client from engine weight, maintaining Expo Go compatibility.
offline_readiness: High within local network. Operates without external internet connectivity as long as local server is reachable.
structured_output_support: Zero native schema support. Emits raw unstructured text; relies entirely on 450+ lines of handwritten regex heuristics in server/src/ocr.ts to populate MedicationOcrDraft.
formulary_grounding_readiness: Moderate. Raw output contains optical errors that require heavy fuzzy phonetic normalization (e.g., Levenshtein/SymSpell) to map to standard Philippine National Drug Formulary (PNDF) codes.
